q01.key_idea: Count the sticks in each shape. The kangaroo has only 3 straight sticks.
steps: The kangaroo has 3 sticks, each as long as the stick in the picture. It cannot break or bend them.
So the shape must be made of exactly 3 straight sticks.
Shapes A, B, C and D each need 4 sticks.
Shape E is 3 sticks that cross in the middle, like a star.

choice_feedback.A: This star has 4 sticks: one across, one up and down, and two slanted ones.
choice_feedback.B: This shape has 4 sticks: 2 standing up and 2 slanted ones.
choice_feedback.C: This shape needs 4 sticks, and the kangaroo has only 3.
choice_feedback.D: This shape needs 4 sticks, and the kangaroo has only 3.

q02.key_idea: Read the top of each mushroom on the ruler, then subtract.
steps: Follow the dashed line from the top of the tall mushroom to the ruler. It is at 11.
Follow the dashed line from the top of the short mushroom to the ruler. It is at 6.
The difference is 11 - 6 = 5.

choice_feedback.A: Count again on the ruler: 11 - 6 = 5, not 4.
choice_feedback.C: 6 is the height of the short mushroom, not the difference.
choice_feedback.D: 11 is the height of the tall mushroom, not the difference.
choice_feedback.E: 17 is 11 + 6. We need to take away, not add.

q03.key_idea: Count the small grid steps along each path.
steps: Each path is made of short pieces, each one square side long. Count them.
Path A has 15 pieces. Path B has 13.
Path C has 12, path D has 12 and path E has 11.
15 is the biggest, so path A is the longest.

choice_feedback.B: Path B has 13 pieces, fewer than 15.
choice_feedback.C: Path C has 12 pieces, fewer than 15.
choice_feedback.D: Path D has 12 pieces, fewer than 15.
choice_feedback.E: Path E has 11 pieces. It is the shortest.

q04.key_idea: The hole must be inside every one of the 4 pieces of paper.
steps: Look at the front piece of paper, at the bottom. Points A and B are above it, so they miss it.
Point C is too far left. It misses the piece at the back on the right.
Point E is too far right. It misses the piece at the back on the left.
Point D is inside all 4 pieces of paper.

choice_feedback.A: Point A is above the front piece of paper, so the hole misses it.
choice_feedback.B: Point B is above the front piece of paper, so the hole misses it.
choice_feedback.C: Point C is to the left of the back piece on the right, so the hole misses it.
choice_feedback.E: Point E is to the right of the back piece on the left, so the hole misses it.

q05.key_idea: A mirror flips the whole picture: the order of the digits turns around and each digit is flipped too.
steps: On the shirt it says 2021.
In a mirror, the last digit, 1, shows up first on the left. So we see the digits in the order 1, 2, 0, 2.
Each digit is also flipped, so the 1 and both 2s face the other way.
Picture A has the order 1, 2, 0, 2 with every digit flipped.

choice_feedback.B: If you flip this back, it says 1202, not 2021.
choice_feedback.C: If you flip this back, it says 2120, not 2021.
choice_feedback.D: The order is turned around, but the 1 and the first 2 are not flipped.
choice_feedback.E: The order is turned around, but the 1 and the last 2 are not flipped.

q06.key_idea: Put the towers in order from shortest to tallest.
steps: The pink tower is taller than the red tower: red, pink.
The pink tower is shorter than the green tower: red, pink, green.
The silver tower is taller than the green tower: red, pink, green, silver.
The silver tower is at the end of the line, so it is the tallest.

choice_feedback.A: The green tower is taller than the pink tower.
choice_feedback.B: The silver tower is taller than the green tower.
choice_feedback.C: The red tower is the shortest of all.
choice_feedback.E: The clues put all 4 towers in order, so we can decide.

q07.key_idea: Check which side each child's right hand is on: it depends on which way the child faces.
steps: There are 7 children. The 5 children in the middle hold hands on both sides, so each of them uses the right hand. That is 5.
The girl at the left end faces us. Her right hand is on our left, and it is free.
The girl at the right end faces us too. Her right hand is on our left, and she is holding hands with it.
So 5 + 1 = 6 children hold a hand with their right hand.

choice_feedback.A: Count again: every child in the middle uses both hands.
choice_feedback.B: Count again: every child in the middle uses both hands.
choice_feedback.C: Count again: every child in the middle uses both hands.
choice_feedback.D: You forgot the girl at the right end. She holds hands with her right hand.

q08.key_idea: Check both rules: every number must be bigger than 3, and the sum must be 20.
steps: Look for stars with 1, 2 or 3. C has 3 and 2, D has 1, and E has 2. They are out.
A has 5, 7, 4 and 6. 5 + 7 + 4 + 6 = 22. That is not 20.
B has 5, 8 and 7. All are bigger than 3, and 5 + 8 + 7 = 20.

choice_feedback.A: All numbers are bigger than 3, but 5 + 7 + 4 + 6 = 22, not 20.
choice_feedback.C: This one has a 3 and a 2. They are not bigger than 3.
choice_feedback.D: This one has a 1. It is not bigger than 3.
choice_feedback.E: This one has a 2. It is not bigger than 3.

q09.key_idea: Each cut across the ribbon makes one more piece.
steps: Follow the dashed line from the scissors down to the bottom.
Count every place where the line crosses the ribbon. Some parts of the ribbon are very close together, so go slowly. There are 11 crossings.
One ribbon cut in 1 place makes 2 pieces. Each cut adds 1 more piece.
So 11 cuts make 11 + 1 = 12 pieces.

choice_feedback.A: Count the crossings again. There are 11 of them.
choice_feedback.B: Count the crossings again. There are 11 of them.
choice_feedback.C: 11 is the number of cuts. The ribbon has 1 more piece than cuts.
choice_feedback.E: There are 11 cuts, so there are 12 pieces, not 13.

q10.key_idea: Add up the lengths of the walls as Rose walks around.
steps: From B, Rose walks 4 m to C, then 1 m to D, then 5 m to E, then 2 m to A, then 3 m back to B.
One whole lap is 4 + 1 + 5 + 2 + 3 = 15 m.
She still has 20 - 15 = 5 m to walk.
She walks 4 m to C and 1 more m to D. That makes 5 m, so she stops at D.

choice_feedback.A: She passes A after 12 m, but she keeps walking.
choice_feedback.B: She is back at B after 15 m, but she still has 5 m to go.
choice_feedback.C: She reaches C the second time after 19 m. She still has 1 m to go.
choice_feedback.E: She passes E after 10 m, but she keeps walking.

q11.key_idea: Find how many more goals Angela scored, then turn goals into points.
steps: Angela scored 9 goals and Julie scored 5 goals.
Angela scored 9 - 5 = 4 more goals.
Each goal is 2 points, so 4 goals are 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8 points.

choice_feedback.A: 4 is how many more goals, not how many more points.
choice_feedback.B: Each goal is 2 points, so 4 more goals give 8 more points.
choice_feedback.D: 10 is Julie's points. Angela has 18 points, which is 8 more.
choice_feedback.E: Angela has 18 points and Julie has 10. 18 - 10 = 8.

q12.key_idea: In each pot, make the number of gray, white and black flowers the same.
steps: Count the left pot: 4 gray, 2 white and 2 black flowers.
To make every kind 4, Julia adds 2 white and 2 black flowers. That is 4 flowers.
Count the right pot: 1 gray, 4 white and 3 black flowers.
To make every kind 4, she adds 3 gray and 1 black flower. That is 4 more flowers.
In total she buys 4 + 4 = 8 flowers.

choice_feedback.A: 3 flowers are not enough to fix even one pot.
choice_feedback.B: 4 flowers fix only one pot. The other pot needs 4 too.
choice_feedback.C: Count again: each pot needs 4 new flowers.
choice_feedback.E: She can do it with fewer: 4 + 4 = 8 is enough.

review.note: Stem is ambiguous. 'Each pot has the same number of each type of flower' can be read as the two pots matching each other (needs 6, which is not a choice) or as all three kinds being equal inside each pot (needs 4 + 4 = 8, key D). The blind solver and these steps use the inside-each-pot reading. Consider rewording the stem.

q13.key_idea: Each number in the code is the row of that letter on the board.
steps: In PIZZA, P is in row 2, I is in row 4, Z is in row 1 and A is in row 2. So the code tells the row.
Code 3 2 4 2 means: a letter from row 3, then row 2, then row 4, then row 2.
MATH: M is in row 3, A in row 2, T in row 4 and H in row 2. It fits.

choice_feedback.A: In MAZE, Z and E are in row 1, so the code is 3 2 1 1.
choice_feedback.B: In MASK, S is in row 3 and K is in row 1, so the code is 3 2 3 1.
choice_feedback.C: In MILK, I and L are in row 4 and K is in row 1, so the code is 3 4 4 1.
choice_feedback.D: In MATE, E is in row 1, so the code ends with 1, not 2.

q14.key_idea: Find where each piece fits, matching every little square.
steps: The 2 pieces have 5 circles, 5 diamonds and 6 plus signs in all. Figure E has only 4 circles, so it is out.
In figure A, turn the U-shaped piece on its side so it opens to the right. It covers the top row's first 3 squares, the left side and the bottom row's first 3 squares.
Turn the other piece upside down. Its long side fills the right edge of figure A, and its 2 by 2 block fills the middle.
Every square matches, so the 2 pieces make figure A.

choice_feedback.B: The U-shaped piece does not fit anywhere in this figure.
choice_feedback.C: The U-shaped piece fits along the bottom, but the other piece does not fit in the space that is left.
choice_feedback.D: Neither piece fits anywhere in this figure.
choice_feedback.E: This figure has 4 circles and 6 diamonds. The pieces have 5 circles and 5 diamonds.

q15.key_idea: Follow each path to see whose house each friend walks past.
steps: Two children walk past Leo's house. On the right, the paths from the green house and the peach house join and go past the blue-green house. So the blue-green house is Leo's.
Doris and Ali live in the green house and the peach house.
On the left, the path from the yellow house with the orange roof goes past the light brown house with the gray roof.
Eva walks past Chloe's house, so Eva lives in the yellow house.

choice_feedback.A: The peach house's path goes past Leo's house. This is Doris's or Ali's house.
choice_feedback.C: The green house's path goes past Leo's house. This is Doris's or Ali's house.
choice_feedback.D: Two children walk past the blue-green house. It is Leo's house.
choice_feedback.E: The yellow house's path goes past this house. It is Chloe's house.

q16.key_idea: What the kangaroo eats from the second branch is what was left on the first branch.
steps: Try an example. The kangaroo eats 3 leaves from the first branch. 10 - 3 = 7 leaves are left there.
Then it eats 7 leaves from the second branch. 10 - 7 = 3 leaves are left there.
Together 7 + 3 = 10 leaves are left.
Try another number, like 4: 6 are left, then 4 are left. 6 + 4 = 10 again.

choice_feedback.A: Try an example: 7 + 3 = 10 leaves are left, not 5.
choice_feedback.B: Try an example: 7 + 3 = 10 leaves are left, not 6.
choice_feedback.C: Try an example: 7 + 3 = 10 leaves are left, not 8.
choice_feedback.E: There were only 20 leaves, and the kangaroo ate 10 of them. So 10 are left, not 15.

q17.key_idea: Find a place in the square for each shape. The one with no place was not used.
steps: Turn shape E so its arrows point right. The 3 arrows fill the top 3 squares of the right column, and its 2 circles fill the last 2 squares of the bottom row.
Shape B fits as it is: its 3 diamonds go in the third column, and its circle goes next to the bottom diamond.
Turn shape A: it fills the top left corner with 3 stars and 1 diamond.
Turn shape C: it fills the bottom left corner with 2 stars and 1 circle.
Now the square is full, and shape D was not used.

choice_feedback.A: Shape A is used. Turned, it fills the top left corner.
choice_feedback.B: Shape B is used. It fills the third column and the circle next to it.
choice_feedback.C: Shape C is used. Turned, it fills the bottom left corner.
choice_feedback.E: Shape E is used. Turned, its arrows go down the right side.

q18.key_idea: Keep changing fruit until no more changes can be made.
steps: She starts with 4 apples and 5 bananas.
3 apples become 1 banana. Now she has 1 apple and 6 bananas.
3 bananas become 1 apple, two times. Now she has 3 apples and 0 bananas.
3 apples become 1 banana. Now she has just 1 banana, and she cannot change any more.

choice_feedback.B: She has 1 apple in the middle of the changes, but she still has bananas to change then.
choice_feedback.C: She never has 1 apple and 1 banana at the same time.
choice_feedback.D: She never ends with 2 bananas. Follow the changes one by one.
choice_feedback.E: When she gets 3 apples, she must change them into 1 banana.

q19.key_idea: Add all the cards, then split the sum in half.
steps: Both boxes have the same sum, so each box has 10.
The box with 4 needs 10 - 4 = 6 more.
The only way to make 6 with the other cards is the card 6. So 6 is in the box with 4.

choice_feedback.A: With 2 the box would need 4 more, and there is no other 4.
choice_feedback.B: With 3 the box would need 3 more, and there is no other 3.
choice_feedback.C: 4 + 5 = 9, and no card is 1. So 5 goes in the other box.
choice_feedback.E: We can decide: only the card 6 makes the box with 4 add up to 10.

q20.key_idea: Count teeth: when the small cog turns once, the big cog turns only half way.
steps: The small cog has 8 teeth. The big cog has 16 teeth.
When the small cog makes one full turn, 8 teeth of the big cog go past. 8 is half of 16, so the big cog turns half way around.
The small black tooth comes back to where it started, next to the big cog.
The big black tooth goes half way around, so it ends up on the opposite side, at the bottom right.

choice_feedback.A: This is how they start. The big cog turns too, so its black tooth moves.
choice_feedback.B: The big black tooth has gone only part of the way. It must go half way around.
choice_feedback.D: The big black tooth has moved only a little. It must go half way around.
choice_feedback.E: The big black tooth is not on the opposite side from where it started.

q21.key_idea: Each girl dances once with each boy, and each dance takes 1 minute.
steps: Each girl dances with 2 boys. That is 2 dances for each girl.
There are 3 girls, so 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 dances.
Only one pair dances at a time, and each dance is 1 minute. So they dance 6 minutes.

choice_feedback.A: 5 is the number of children, not the number of dances.
choice_feedback.C: Count the pairs again: 3 girls with 2 boys each make 6 pairs.
choice_feedback.D: Count the pairs again: 3 girls with 2 boys each make 6 pairs.
choice_feedback.E: Count the pairs again: 3 girls with 2 boys each make 6 pairs.

q22.key_idea: Find the cookie that runs out first: the moon.
steps: Each tray has just 1 moon cookie.
The plate has 3 moon cookies, so we need at least 3 trays.
3 trays have plenty of the other cookies: 9 pink stars, 6 big pointy stars, 9 triangles and 6 hearts.
The plate needs only 4 pink stars, 3 big pointy stars, 2 triangles and 2 hearts. So 3 trays are enough.

choice_feedback.A: 1 tray has only 1 moon, but the plate has 3 moons.
choice_feedback.B: 2 trays have only 2 moons, but the plate has 3 moons.
choice_feedback.D: 3 trays are already enough, so 4 is not the smallest.
choice_feedback.E: 3 trays are already enough, so 5 is not the smallest.

q23.key_idea: Count the fruit for one week, then double it.
steps: Monday, Wednesday and Friday: 2 apples each day. 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.
Tuesday and Thursday: 3 mangoes each day. 3 + 3 = 6.
Saturday and Sunday: nothing. So one week is 6 + 6 = 12.
Two weeks: 12 + 12 = 24.

choice_feedback.A: 12 is for one week only. We need two weeks.
choice_feedback.B: One week is 12, so two weeks are 12 + 12 = 24.
choice_feedback.C: One week is 12, so two weeks are 12 + 12 = 24.
choice_feedback.D: One week is 12, so two weeks are 12 + 12 = 24.

q24.key_idea: Find where the ball can go, then see which shelves stay free for the puzzle.
steps: The blocks are below the ball, and the game and the car are above it. So the ball is on shelf 2 or 3.
Ball on 2: blocks on 1, game on 3, and the car and the puzzle share 4 and 5.
Ball on 3: game on 4, car on 5, and the blocks and the puzzle share 1 and 2.
The puzzle can go on 1, 2, 4 or 5, but never on shelf 3.

choice_feedback.A: The puzzle can be on 1: ball on 3, game on 4, car on 5, blocks on 2.
choice_feedback.B: The puzzle can be on 2: ball on 3, game on 4, car on 5, blocks on 1.
choice_feedback.D: The puzzle can be on 4: ball on 2, game on 3, car on 5, blocks on 1.
choice_feedback.E: The puzzle can be on 5: ball on 2, game on 3, car on 4, blocks on 1.
